욥기-39-1.title: 욥기 39장 1절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-1.exegesis: 41. Lu 12:24 . Transition from the noble lioness to the croaking raven. Though man dislikes it, as of ill omen, God cares for it, as for all His creatures.
욥기-39-1.theologicalNote: 41. Lu 12:24 . Transition from the noble lioness to the croaking raven. Though man dislikes it, as of ill omen, God cares for it, as for all His creatures.

욥기-39-2.title: 욥기 39장 2절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 39 Job 39:1-30 . 1. Even wild beasts, cut off from all care of man, are cared for by God at their seasons of greatest need. Their instinct comes direct from God and guides them to help themselves in parturition; the very time when the herdsman is most anxious for his herds. wild goats-- ibex ( Psa 104:18 ; 1Sa 24:2 ). hinds-- fawns; most timid and defenseless animals, yet cared for by God.

욥기-39-3.title: 욥기 39장 3절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-3.exegesis: 2. They bring forth with ease and do not need to reckon the months of pregnancy, as the shepherd does in the case of his flocks.
욥기-39-3.theologicalNote: 2. They bring forth with ease and do not need to reckon the months of pregnancy, as the shepherd does in the case of his flocks.

욥기-39-4.title: 욥기 39장 4절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-4.exegesis: 3. bow themselves-- in parturition; bend on their knees ( 1Sa 4:19 ). bring forth-- literally, "cause their young to cleave the womb and break forth." sorrows-- their young ones, the cause of their momentary pains.
욥기-39-4.theologicalNote: 3. bow themselves-- in parturition; bend on their knees ( 1Sa 4:19 ). bring forth-- literally, "cause their young to cleave the womb and break forth." sorrows-- their young ones, the cause of their momentary pains.

욥기-39-5.title: 욥기 39장 5절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-5.exegesis: 4. are in good liking-- in good condition, grow up strong. with corn-- rather, "in the field," without man's care. return not-- being able to provide for themselves.
욥기-39-5.theologicalNote: 4. are in good liking-- in good condition, grow up strong. with corn-- rather, "in the field," without man's care. return not-- being able to provide for themselves.

욥기-39-6.title: 욥기 39장 6절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-6.exegesis: 5. wild ass-- Two different Hebrew words are here used for the same animal, "the ass of the woods" and "the wild ass." (See on Job 6:5 ; Job 11:12 ; Job 24:5 ; and Jr 2:24 ). loosed the bands-- given its liberty to. Man can rob animals of freedom, but not, as God, give freedom, combined with subordination to fixed laws.

욥기-39-7.title: 욥기 39장 7절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-7.exegesis: 6. barren-- literally, "salt," that is, unfruitful. (So Psa 107:34 , Margin.)
욥기-39-7.theologicalNote: 6. barren-- literally, "salt," that is, unfruitful. (So Psa 107:34 , Margin.)

욥기-39-8.title: 욥기 39장 8절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-8.exegesis: 7. multitude-- rather, "din"; he sets it at defiance, being far away from it in the freedom of the wilderness. driver-- who urges on the tame ass to work. The wild ass is the symbol of uncontrolled freedom in the East; even kings have, therefore, added its name to them.
욥기-39-8.theologicalNote: 7. multitude-- rather, "din"; he sets it at defiance, being far away from it in the freedom of the wilderness. driver-- who urges on the tame ass to work. The wild ass is the symbol of uncontrolled freedom in the East; even kings have, therefore, added its name to them.

욥기-39-9.title: 욥기 39장 9절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-9.exegesis: 8. The range-- literally, "searching," "that which it finds by searching is his pasture."
욥기-39-9.theologicalNote: 8. The range-- literally, "searching," "that which it finds by searching is his pasture."

욥기-39-10.title: 욥기 39장 10절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-10.exegesis: 9. unicorn-- Pliny [Natural History, 8.21], mentions such an animal; its figure is found depicted in the ruins of Persepolis. The Hebrew reem conveys the idea of loftiness and power (compare Ramah; Indian, Ram; Latin, Roma). The rhinoceros was perhaps the original type of the unicorn. The Arab rim is a two-horned animal. Sometimes "unicorn" or reem is a mere poetical symbol or abstraction; but the buffalo is the animal referred to here, from the contrast to the tame ox, used in ploughing ( Job 39:10 , 12 ). abide-- literally, "pass the night." crib-- ( Is 1:3 ).

욥기-39-11.title: 욥기 39장 11절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-11.exegesis: 10. his band-- fastened to the horns, as its chief strength lies in the head and shoulders. after thee-- obedient to thee; willing to follow, instead of being goaded on before thee.
욥기-39-11.theologicalNote: 10. his band-- fastened to the horns, as its chief strength lies in the head and shoulders. after thee-- obedient to thee; willing to follow, instead of being goaded on before thee.

욥기-39-13.title: 욥기 39장 13절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-13.exegesis: 12. believe-- trust. seed-- produce ( 1Sa 8:15 ). into thy barn-- rather, "gather (the contents of) thy threshing-floor" [Maurer]; the corn threshed on it.
욥기-39-13.theologicalNote: 12. believe-- trust. seed-- produce ( 1Sa 8:15 ). into thy barn-- rather, "gather (the contents of) thy threshing-floor" [Maurer]; the corn threshed on it.

욥기-39-14.title: 욥기 39장 14절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-14.exegesis: 13. Rather, "the wing of the ostrich hen"-- literally, "the crying bird"; as the Arab name for it means "song"; referring to its night cries ( Job 30:29 ; Mi 1:8 ) vibrating joyously. "Is it not like the quill and feathers of the pious bird" (the stork)? [Umbreit]. The vibrating, quivering wing, serving for sail and oar at once, is characteristic of the ostrich in full course. Its white and black feathers in the wing and tail are like the stork's. But, unlike that bird, the symbol of parental love in the East, it with seeming want of natural (pious) affection deserts its young. Both birds are poetically called by descriptive, instead of their usual appellative, names.

욥기-39-15.title: 욥기 39장 15절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-15.exegesis: 14-15. Yet (unlike the stork) she "leaveth," &c. Hence called by the Arabs "the impious bird." However, the fact is, she lays her eggs with great care and hatches them, as other birds do; but in hot countries the eggs do not need so constant incubation; she therefore often leaves them and sometimes forgets the place on her return. Moreover, the outer eggs, intended for food, she feeds to her young; these eggs, lying separate in the sand, exposed to the sun, gave rise to the idea of her altogether leaving them. God describes her as she seems to man; implying, though she may seem foolishly to neglect her young, yet really she is guided by a sure instinct from God, as much as animals of instincts widely different.

욥기-39-17.title: 욥기 39장 17절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-17.exegesis: 16. On a slight noise she often forsakes her eggs, and returns not, as if she were "hardened towards her young." her labour-- in producing eggs, is in vain, (yet) she has not disquietude (about her young), unlike other birds, who, if one egg and another are taken away, will go on laying till their full number is made up.

욥기-39-18.title: 욥기 39장 18절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-18.exegesis: 17. wisdom-- such as God gives to other animals, and to man ( Job 35:11 ). The Arab proverb is, "foolish as an ostrich." Yet her very seeming want of wisdom is not without wise design of God, though man cannot see it; just as in the trials of the godly, which seem so unreasonable to Job, there lies hid a wise design.

욥기-39-19.title: 욥기 39장 19절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-19.exegesis: 18. Notwithstanding her deficiencies, she has distinguishing excellences. lifteth ... herself-- for running; she cannot mount in the air. Gesenius translates: "lashes herself" up to her course by flapping her wings. The old versions favor English Version, and the parallel "scorneth" answers to her proudly "lifting up herself."

욥기-39-20.title: 욥기 39장 20절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-20.exegesis: 19. The allusion to "the horse" ( Job 39:18 ), suggests the description of him. Arab poets delight in praising the horse; yet it is not mentioned in the possessions of Job ( Job 1:3 ; 42:12). It seems to have been at the time chiefly used for war, rather than "domestic purposes." thunder-- poetically for, "he with arched neck inspires fear as thunder does." Translate, "majesty" [Umbreit]. Rather "the trembling, quivering mane," answering to the "vibrating wing" of the ostrich (see on Job 39:13 ) [Maurer]. "Mane" in Greek also is from a root meaning "fear." English Version is more sublime.

욥기-39-21.title: 욥기 39장 21절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-21.exegesis: 20. make ... afraid-- rather, "canst thou (as I do) make him spring as the locust?" So in Joe 2:4 , the comparison is between locusts and war-horses. The heads of the two are so similar that the Italians call the locusts cavaletta, "little horse." nostrils-- snorting furiously.

욥기-39-22.title: 욥기 39장 22절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-22.exegesis: 21. valley-- where the battle is joined. goeth on-- goeth forth ( Nu 1:3 ; 21:23).
욥기-39-22.theologicalNote: 21. valley-- where the battle is joined. goeth on-- goeth forth ( Nu 1:3 ; 21:23).

욥기-39-23.title: 욥기 39장 23절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-23.exegesis: 21. valley-- where the battle is joined. goeth on-- goeth forth ( Nu 1:3 ; 21:23).

욥기-39-24.title: 욥기 39장 24절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-24.exegesis: 23. quiver-- for the arrows, which they contain, and which are directed "against him." glittering spear-- literally, "glittering of the spear," like "lightning of the spear" ( Ha 3:11 ). shield-- rather, "lance."

욥기-39-25.title: 욥기 39장 25절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-25.exegesis: 24. swalloweth-- Fretting with impatience, he draws the ground towards him with his hoof, as if he would swallow it. The parallelism shows this to be the sense; not as Maurer, "scours over it." neither believeth-- for joy. Rather, "he will not stand still, when the note of the trumpet (soundeth)."

욥기-39-26.title: 욥기 39장 26절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-26.exegesis: 25. saith-- poetically applied to his mettlesome neighing, whereby he shows his love of the battle. smelleth-- snuffeth; discerneth ( Is 11:3 , Margin). thunder-- thundering voice.

욥기-39-27.title: 욥기 39장 27절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-27.exegesis: 26. The instinct by which some birds migrate to warmer climes before winter. Rapid flying peculiarly characterizes the whole hawk genus.
욥기-39-27.theologicalNote: 26. The instinct by which some birds migrate to warmer climes before winter. Rapid flying peculiarly characterizes the whole hawk genus.

욥기-39-28.title: 욥기 39장 28절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-28.exegesis: 27. eagle-- It flies highest of all birds: thence called "the bird of heaven."
욥기-39-28.theologicalNote: 27. eagle-- It flies highest of all birds: thence called "the bird of heaven."

욥기-39-29.title: 욥기 39장 29절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-29.exegesis: 28. abideth-- securely ( Psa 91:1 ); it occupies the same abode mostly for life. crag-- literally, "tooth" ( 1Sa 14:5 , Margin). strong place-- citadel, fastness.

욥기-39-30.title: 욥기 39장 30절 역사문법적 주해
욥기-39-30.exegesis: 29. seeketh-- is on the lookout for. behold-- The eagle descries its prey at an astonishing distance, by sight, rather than smell.
